messages:
derek: Heads-up — after last night's driver bump (NVDriver 554.12) we are seeing a small-seq kernel flip on H100 pools. p95 token latency ~2x on low-latency routes. KV-cache hit distribution also oscillating.

sarah: Which model / seq length distribution? can you paste a quick perf sample? :eyes:

derek: quick paste from flame/profiler: ```kernel_choice: binary: smallseq->vectorized_slowpath
seq=8: 72% vectorized_slowpath (latency 18ms)
seq=8 legacy_smallseq: 28% (latency 9ms)
kvcache_hit_rate: 0.87 -> 0.64 post-bump
request_tail_p95: 42ms -> 85ms```

maria: yikes. I see similar in our nightly: small batches (1-2 requests) flip to slowpath when driver reports different occupancy heuristics. looks like kernel autotuner tie-break now prefers the new kernel on this driver ABI.

aj: oncall — impact? customer-facing errors or just latency?

derek: only latency right now, CPU/GPU utilization not saturated. Hard regress on latency-sensitive routes — important for realtime customers.

sarah: can we force the selector back temporarily? any runtime flag?

derek: yes — we have a selector override env we can use for canary: ```RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=force:legacy_smallseq``` This forces pick for small-seq paths at process start. I tested on a dev shard, p95 dropped back to ~10ms.

maria: nice. We should avoid full fleet restart if possible. Suggest canary: pick 10% of H100 capacity in us-west-2, set override on those pods and run traffic replay for 30m. watch p50/p95, kv hit rate, and kernel_choice histogram.

aj: rollback driver to previous build is another option but heavy (reboot hosts). prefer runtime override + canary.

sarah: agree. ops: how hard to patch the node agent to set env for just canary slice?

derek: ~15m to create a deployment patch and annotate rollout. I'll coordinate with ops. plan: 1) create canary cluster group (10%); 2) patch runtime env to RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=force:legacy_smallseq; 3) monitor 30m; 4) if green, roll 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m waits.

maria: add a short-term heuristic tweak too — we can change selector bias value without restart: ```curl -XPOST http://runtime-config/api/v1/update -d '{"kernel_selector.small_seq_bias":"+6"}'``` That nudges the scoring to prefer legacy without full force. we should use both: override for immediate relief and bias change for lower-disruption roll.

aj: please ensure rollback plan if canary shows degradation: either revert env OR revert bias. also prepare driver rollback runbook if needed.

derek: noted. I'll open a quick PR for the canary patch and post link.

sarah: deploy-bot can you schedule a canary rollout window and post a deploy ticket?

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary patch queued for 2023-11-09T02:10:00Z (ticket #INF-7423). automated smoke tests will run post-deploy.

maria: metrics to watch: kernel_choice_distribution, kvcache_hit_rate, token_p95, request_tail_rate, evictions/sec. alert if kvcache_hit_rate drops >5% or token_p95 increases >20% from baseline.

aj: assign owners: derek -> canary rollout + PR, sarah -> ops coordination, maria -> perf monitoring and smoke tests.

derek: I'll start the PR and canary now. ETA 40m to first canary. Will post logs and brief results here.

sarah: thanks team. if canary fails, we'll either revert the env or escalate to driver rollback. keep comms tight.

maria: also capturing profiler traces (nvprof-like) and kernel symbols if we need to file an infra bug with driver vendor.

derek: posted initial smoke after patch: p95 on canary back to 11ms, kvcache_hit_rate 0.86. Holding for 30m.

aj: ack. monitoring. :thumbsup:
